bear_case.title: China dominates cells
bear_case.description: A fresh analysis this week found CATL's grid-storage (ESS) battery revenue actually fell 1% in H1 2026 even as shipment volumes kept growing, with the tariff impact on that gap still unclear — a reminder that Chinese cell makers are absorbing margin pressure to defend share rather than ceding it. CATL and BYD together still dominate global cell manufacturing scale; North America/Europe/other reaching 56% of ESS shipment destinations for the first time is geographic diversification, not a change in who makes the cells.

bear_case.title: Policy whiplash is already claiming casualties
bear_case.description: Wood Mackenzie now projects an 11% contraction in the US utility-scale storage market in 2026 and a further 8% decline in 2027 as FEOC content restrictions (in force since Jan 1, 2026) and Section 301 tariffs bottleneck FEOC-compliant equipment and safe-harbored capacity — even as the firm still expects the market to quadruple toward ~200GW/655GWh cumulative by 2031 once domestic manufacturing, like LG Energy Solution's newly opened 35GWh Lansing, MI plant, comes fully online. Over $32B of US clean-energy storage projects were already canceled or downsized in 2025, and integrator Powin's Chapter 11 liquidation remains the clearest casualty to date.

bear_case.title: Margin compression
bear_case.description: Eos Energy is this week's starkest evidence: a Q2 net loss that widened to $275.7M, a tightened FY26 revenue guide ($300–350M from $300–400M), and new securities-law-firm investigations opened Aug 20. Fluence's analyst base is fracturing in the same direction — GLJ downgraded to Hold and Citi trimmed its own target to $20 from $24 — even as the company's $6.4B backlog says demand isn't the constraint. Software attach (Stem's 55% non-GAAP gross margin) remains the differentiator; hardware stays under real pressure.

bear_case.title: Solid-state timelines
bear_case.description: QuantumScape's Cobra-process cells keep shipping to Volkswagen and appeared on the Ducati V21L, but an Aug 18 Scientific American analysis explicitly questioned whether QuantumScape and peers like Factorial Energy can mass-produce solid-state cells at all against Chinese-dominated manufacturing scale — there is still no production license, no volume commitment, and no revenue.
